findings.description: The website glossary says the Policy ADT has "Fourteen variants discriminated on `_tag`". The actual `Policy` union in packages/core/src/Policy.ts has sixteen `_tag` variants (AllOf, AnyOf, HasActed, HasAction, HasAttribute, HasCustom, HasNotActed, HasPermission, HasRelationship, HasResourceAttribute, HasRole, HasSignature, Labeled, Not, Obliged, Rules). The normative spec/glossary.md already says "Sixteen variants" (line 68), and the root README.md correctly says "sixteen policy constructors" — only this website page is stale, apparently not updated when HasCustom (CCR-QD-082) and HasSignature (ADR-QD-058) were added as new leaf variants.
findings.suggestedFix: Change "Fourteen variants" to "Sixteen variants" in the website glossary's Policy entry, matching spec/glossary.md.

findings.description: The `simplify` example shows `const tidy = simplify(verbose)` for `verbose = allOf([allOf([hasRole("editor")])])` producing a comment `// { _tag: "AllOf", policies: [{ _tag: "HasRole", role: "editor" }], ... } — two fewer AllOf wrappers`. This is wrong: per packages/core/src/Simplify.ts, a single-child AllOf/AnyOf collapses fully to its own child (confirmed by packages/core/test/Simplify.test.ts's "unwraps a single-child composite" test: `simplify(P.allOf([P.hasRole("a")]))` deepStrictEqual `P.hasRole("a")`, not an AllOf wrapping it). Applying that twice to the doubly-nested single-child example yields a bare `{ _tag: "HasRole", role: "editor" }` with zero AllOf wrappers, not one. The accompanying "before/after" SVG diagram earlier in the same file repeats the same wrong picture (an AllOf still wrapping HasRole in the "AFTER" box). Since this is a `typescript` fence, check-doc-examples.mjs type-checks it but does not execute it or verify the comment, so this runtime-behavior error is undetected by the merge gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the comment (and the SVG's "AFTER" box) to show simplify(verbose) === hasRole("editor") with no AllOf wrapper remaining, or use an example whose outer AllOf has more than one child so a wrapper genuinely survives.

findings.description: The status-mapping table lists only `AttributeResolveError`, `RelationshipResolveError`, `DecisionHistoryUnavailable`, `SubjectExtractionFailed` as mapping to 502. packages/http/src/QadiHttpError.ts's actual `toResponse` Match.tagsExhaustive also maps `CustomPredicateError` and `SignatureHistoryUnavailable` to 502 (added alongside `hasCustom`/`hasSignature`). The website's newer docs/packages/http.md page already lists all five 502-mapped EnforcementError tags correctly; only this package README is stale.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `CustomPredicateError` and `SignatureHistoryUnavailable` to the 502 row of packages/http/README.md's status table, matching apps/website/src/content/docs/docs/packages/http.md and the real Match.tagsExhaustive in QadiHttpError.ts.

findings.description: The inline SVG diagram's label reads `compileSql(predicate, "postgres") →`. The real `compileSql` signature (packages/predicate-sql/src/index.ts, `CompileSqlOptions`) takes an options object, not a bare dialect string: `compileSql(predicate, { dialect: "postgres" })` — confirmed by the correct usage shown in this same page's own runnable example just below and in packages/predicate-sql/README.md. A reader who copies the diagram's call shape would get a type error.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the SVG label to `compileSql(predicate, { dialect: "postgres" }) →` to match the real signature and the page's own code example.

findings.description: The README says "examples/nextjs-newsroom mounts the dock with every one of DevtoolsDockProps' twelve fields wired," and examples/nextjs-newsroom/src/client/Dock.tsx's own doc comment (line 5) states outright "DevtoolsDockProps has twelve optional fields." The interface in packages/devtools/src/react/DevtoolsDock.tsx actually declares thirteen optional fields (source, capacity, catalogue, wiring, activity, portCalls, questions, gates, unknownParents, hydration, hydrationMismatches, onInvalidate, ports). Dock.tsx wires twelve of them (all except `capacity`, which has a sensible default), so "all twelve wired" is accurate but the stated total field count of the interface ("has twelve optional fields") is off by one.
findings.suggestedFix: Say "twelve of the interface's thirteen optional fields" (or similar) in packages/devtools/README.md and examples/nextjs-newsroom/src/client/Dock.tsx, rather than implying DevtoolsDockProps has only twelve fields total.
